Description: Transfers add new-role birthright access but prior-role entitlements are rarely revoked, so privilege creep accumulates across role changes with no manager reaffirmation step.
Leaver de-provisioning runs on a nightly batch from the HR source so the same-day disablement expectation (ASD ISM-0430) is not consistently met for contractors and federated SaaS targets.
Annual certification campaigns run on schedule and most items are decisioned, but no-decision items currently default to retain rather than revoke and revocation actioning often slips past SLA.

Privileged entitlements are flagged within the general campaign but lack a separate shorter cadence and a consistent named-owner sign-off, so the highest-impact access is not validated more often than ordinary access.

Summary: [GAP] Preventive SoD checks at access-request time
Description: Access requests are not evaluated against the SoD ruleset before provisioning, so toxic combinations are only discovered later during detective scans rather than blocked at the source.
A versioned SoD ruleset with named owners exists for the SOX-relevant scope, but the violation-management workflow and time-bound exception re-attestation are only partly documented and applied.

The workflow blocks the trivial requester-equals-approver case, but delegation re-routing is not checked against the requester and application administrators can still edit their own entitlements in admin consoles without detection or alerting; no periodic self-approval audit report is produced.
No agent registry exists; autonomous agents run under shared or over-privileged service accounts with no declared owner or purpose.
Some agent tool-scopes are reviewed during periodic access certification, but there is no continuous attestation and effective agent authority is not resolvable end-to-end.
Account-to-owner reconciliation is performed only on a few critical systems; dormant accounts beyond the inactivity threshold are not systematically detected or disabled estate-wide.
There is no event-driven micro-certification; risk-relevant changes such as transfers or new privileged grants wait for the next scheduled campaign to be re-validated.

Detective SoD scans run on the SOX-critical ERP and core banking systems, but coverage of cross-system toxic pairs and a complete mitigating-control register across the wider estate is still incomplete.
There is no periodic least-privilege right-sizing report driven by usage telemetry; standing excess access is added far more readily than it is removed, with no measured reduction trend.

The request workflow supports time-bound access and some contractor grants carry an expiry, but high-risk entitlements default to perpetual and renewals are waved through without a fresh owner approval, so expiry-driven re-validation is not yet a working control.

Access governance covers applications only; file shares, SharePoint sites and cloud buckets have no owner inventory, sharing links and org-wide grants proliferate unreviewed, and there is no open-access scanning or repository-owner certification.
Decommissioned agents and their consent grants are not systematically detected; orphan-agent population is unmeasured.
